solidworks_assembly_create_exploded_view.doc: Create an explode view of the active assembly configuration from the current mate conditions. It writes one view into the document and does not save it; call it repeatedly to add several views to the same configuration. Read solidworks_assembly_get_exploded_view_count back to prove the create happened, because a perfect result often needs user interaction.

solidworks_assembly_auto_explode.doc: Create one exploded view automatically for the current configuration. It creates only one view per configuration, so use solidworks_assembly_create_exploded_view when you need more. It writes the view into the assembly and does not save the document.

solidworks_assembly_view_explode.doc: Explode the selected exploded view in the display without changing any geometry. Pair it with solidworks_assembly_view_collapse to toggle the display back; it changes no geometry and does not save the document.

solidworks_assembly_view_collapse.doc: Collapse the displayed exploded view back to its assembled position without changing geometry. Pair it with solidworks_assembly_view_explode to toggle the display; it changes no geometry and does not save the document.

solidworks_assembly_show_exploded.doc: Display one named exploded view in the exploded or collapsed position. It changes only the display, changes no geometry and does not save the document; take the view name from solidworks_assembly_get_exploded_view_names.

params.show_it: Whether to show the view exploded: true shows it exploded and false shows it collapsed.
params.explode_view_name: Name of the exploded view to show, taken from solidworks_assembly_get_exploded_view_names.

solidworks_assembly_get_exploded_view_na.doc: List the exploded-view names of one configuration as strings. Read-only; a missing result comes back as an empty list, never as one nameless view.

params.configuration_name: Configuration name to inspect; this takes a configuration name, not an index.

solidworks_assembly_get_exploded_view_co.doc: Get the number of exploded views in one configuration as an integer. Read-only; it is the read-back that proves a create really happened.

params.configuration_name: Configuration name to inspect; this takes a configuration name, not an index.

solidworks_assembly_exploded_view_config.doc: Get the configuration name behind an exploded view by passing the argument through unchanged. Read-only; the official parameter has no documented meaning, so supply the value the official page requires and read the echoed string without interpreting it.

params.arg: Passed through unchanged; the official page documents no meaning for it, so do not read it as an index or as a name.

solidworks_assembly_edit_explode_paramet.doc: Open the explode-parameter editing step of the active assembly. It takes no arguments and modifies the explode parameters; whether it raises an interactive dialog is not determined, so drive it through the repo dialog guard.

solidworks_macro_run.doc: Run a macro procedure from a project file inside the running SolidWorks session. Returns ok, return_value, error_code and error_name, where error_name maps the code through the run-macro error enum; whatever the macro does to the document happens here, and this tool does not save the document. On failure check file_exists first, because a bogus path is the commonest cause and reports error_code 28.

params.file_path: Absolute path of the macro project file, for example a .swp or .swb file.
params.module_name: Module name inside the macro; for a VBA .swp this is the VBA module name, and VSTA .swb semantics are not determined.
params.procedure_name: Procedure name to run, for example main.

solidworks_macro_normalize_model_family.doc: Map a concrete model name onto one of the prompt families this repo uses (gpt, kimi, claude, generic). Internal step of the sw_macro_guard generate_macro_with_guard pipeline; pure string function with no SolidWorks call and no COM.

params.model_name: Model name exactly as written by the caller, for example gpt-4o or claude-3.5-sonnet.

solidworks_macro_build_prompt.doc: Build the prompt that asks a model to write SolidWorks VBA for user_request. Internal step of the sw_macro_guard generate_macro_with_guard pipeline, not meant to be called on its own; it is a pure string function and never calls SolidWorks.

params.user_request: What the user wants the macro to do, in natural language.
params.model_name: Model name mapped onto a prompt family by solidworks_macro_normalize_model_family; empty means the generic family. Defaults to empty.
params.strict: Whether to emit the strict variant of the prompt. Defaults to true.

solidworks_macro_extract_vba_code.doc: Pull the VBA source out of a model reply that mixes prose and code fences. Internal step of the sw_macro_guard generate_macro_with_guard pipeline; pure text handling, no SolidWorks call. Feed the result to solidworks_macro_validate_vba_code before anything runs.

params.text: Raw model output, which may contain prose and Markdown code fences around the code.

solidworks_macro_validate_vba_code.doc: Check a VBA macro against the minimum this repo requires before it is handed to SolidWorks. Pure static pre-flight that runs no code and calls no SolidWorks; it reports the issues it finds, so a non-empty issue list means the macro is not ready to run.

solidworks_macro_select_template.doc: Choose the local VBA template whose keywords match user_request. Internal step of the sw_macro_guard generate_macro_with_guard pipeline; pure function, and the template bodies live in this repo under the MIT licence.

params.user_request: The user's request text, matched against template keywords.

solidworks_macro_fallback_template.doc: Return the local fallback VBA template for user_request, used when model generation fails. Internal step of the sw_macro_guard generate_macro_with_guard pipeline; pure function with no SolidWorks call and no network access.

params.user_request: The user's request text, used to pick the closest template.

solidworks_macro_write_file.doc: Write VBA source to a local file so a human or an agent can load it into SolidWorks. Writes the file, creates its parent directory when missing and resolves the path; it does not run the macro, so use solidworks_macro_run to execute it.

params.output_path: Absolute path to write; a resource path, not a geometry coordinate.

solidworks_costing_evidence.doc: Return the Costing overview of the active part: the body count and whether a cost analysis exists. Read-only; it fails with a reason when the Costing manager or its defaults cannot be read.

solidworks_costing_read_analysis.doc: Read every readable field of the part cost analysis as a dict. Read-only; use it to discover the valid cost-method names, and expect an error when the part has no cost analysis yet.

solidworks_costing_body_count.doc: Return how many bodies Costing sees for the active part. Read-only; cost is computed per body.
